utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom and also those half visible assisting us outside the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Since I see no one standing on their feet, we could -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you never disappoint me. What observation would you like to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a piece of -- I would like to say that indeed the Defence counsel never wishes to disappoint the Chamber. The other point is that the Prosecution has given us details about the videolink, the video conference link that we're going to have, and we should like to say that we shall be responding in the course of next week. I should like to say straight away that all the responses that the Defence is going to make with respect to the accused General Galic, we're going to refer to him as "General Galic." And General Galic is being accused here as the commander, so we shall be referring to him as "General Galic," of course, and not "Mister." thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although you might have noticed, although I have given it some thought, I addressed the accused also as "General Galic," mainly also because it has been done so before and I did not think it wise to change it at that moment. So -- but let me just see. The videolink that we are going to have, as far as I'm aware, we have a motion for videolink. We have a response on that motion. We have no decision yet, as far as I can see. So I do not know exactly what you are referring to, unless there's a new motion. "The Prosecution has given us details about the videolink that we are going to have." That, of course, depends on the decision. "We should like to say that we shall be responding in the course of next week." So if this is just an exchange of practical information between the parties, I'm only too glad to hear that you exchange your views on whatever. But as far as I can see at this moment, we do not expect a response, but we are, rather, preparing a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say was that an additional document has been given to us by the Prosecution with respect to the issues that you, Mr. President, yourself raised, and I think that it quotes a certain number of decisions. And that is what I wanted to respond to, with perhaps some additional explanations, Mr. President. I wasn't speaking of the decision itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. You may recall that I think last Friday I indicated that we were filing some material in response to the queries that you raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I saw that. Mainly apart from some reference to case law indicating that you would further inquire a lot of matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not giving much else at this moment. Yes, I do understand what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I just have one further thing, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There's an additional filing - I think it's been filed already, but I'll check during the morning break - where we seek to add to the initial application, but I will clarify that with you after the morning break. It may be also that my friend is referring to that. Whilst I'm on my feet, yesterday, Mr. President, you said that you could not locate the notice in relation to the three photographs of the front-end loader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think that's in the letter dated 25th of January, 2002, on page 2, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I think these issues having coped with, we could continue with the cross-examination of the witness, Mr. Velic. Could you please bring in the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I continue the cross-examination, of course, with the Court's permission, my colleague would like to ask some additional questions, that is to say Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when I finish my own cross-examination, if -- with the Court's permission, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I have indicated before, usually it's one counsel that does the cross-examination. On the other hand, if it's very limited in time, I do not see specifically why you couldn't do it, just as I do not see any -- do I see that you would take over some additional questions? Okay. Thank you. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Velic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I do understand that you hear me in a language which you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you made a solemn declaration yesterday and that you are still bound by the solemn declaration while being examined today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I still stand by the declaration I made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, now, Ms. Pilipovic will continue to examine you. Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we left off yesterday with an explanation of the position of Grbavica stadium, and you had before you photograph P3244. Do you remember that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: My question for you now is the following: On the photograph, you marked in the cover that existed from the snipers and the UNPROFOR vehicle. Now, the vehicle that you yourself drove -- in addition to the vehicle you drove, were there any other vehicles in this area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just the two UNPROFOR vehicles, my own vehicle and another truck that I was supposed to load the rubbish on to, but it was further off.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a FAP truck, which takes away the rubbish to the depot, to the rubbish dump, when I load it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me the colour of that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was yellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your company, and it was called Rad, the company you worked in, apart from the vehicle that you drove, the loader, were there any other drivers who drove that particular front loader in addition to yourself?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they all had duties with the BH Army, they were all younger men. They were in the army at the time. I was the only one who was a little older, and I had my other work -- work assignments within the company.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that when you didn't drive the loader yourself, nobody else drove it in 1992, 1993 and 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, I drove the loader myself. I was the only one who drove the vehicle, and that was the only vehicle we had, whereas in 1993, I also drove the vehicle myself until the time that I was wounded, and after I had been wounded, the vehicle couldn't be driven either, it was incapacitated, and then they got another vehicle that they used.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the Sarajevo area, were there any other work organisations with vehicles of that kind?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Your loader, can it load up earth as well, in addition to rubbish?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you happen to know that while were you in charge of your vehicle and assigned the vehicle, was it used to load up earth?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. While the war was on, from 1992, quite definitely not. We did no other work with the loader. We just used it to load up the rubbish.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the locality of your company, where your company was situated, were there any other work organisations in that part of Sarajevo, in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was one of them the construction firm called Vranica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, 1993 and 1994, do you happen to know whether that company was used for the production of military materiel and equipment and that some, that soldiers were put up there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't have any information of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In that part of town - and when I say that part of town I'm thinking about Cengic Vila, the Cengic Vila district, which is where you lived as well and where your company was located - were there buildings and facilities which in 1992, 1993, and 1994, were used for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, perhaps just the ZTO. I know that the police was up there. Now, whether the army was there as well, I don't know, though that was what was closest to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, asked by my learned colleague, you said that in November, 1992, a shelling occurred. Could you tell us now, please, where that shelling took place?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it took place all over town. There was shelling all over town. Now, if you want me to be more specific, in the area I lived in, all I can say is that I saw a woman being injured by the explosion of a shell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you happened to know what was targeted with -- what that shell was targeting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what do you want me to say? People had weapons, and whenever they felt like it, or almost, that was a rule, whenever they felt like it, they would press the trigger and fire, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us more specifically which part of town this occurred, the incident you saw occurred, and please situate it with respect to Vranica Transport, the Vranica Transport Company and your own company?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's rather difficult. If the -- they start -- if they have been shooting in one part of town, then they would move to another part of town and shoot in another place, and the Vranica place was one of these and there were some shells that we called roses, we referred to them as roses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us whether you yourself were able to determine which direction the shell came from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we looked at the covers set up by the buildings. For example, if a shell fell in front of my building, from the railway station, there were four high-rise buildings so it couldn't have come from Brace but Zuc, and if it fell by the Miljacka River, then we assumed that it was fired from Grbavica, Vrace and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that there were shells coming from Zuc as well?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Zuc. In 1993, Zuc hadn't been liberated yet, so yes, they were coming from there, some of those elevations as they were called. They called them elevations. I don't know, Golo Brdo, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, you said that you were up at the front lines digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we went to dig trenches manually.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how far the line controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska were from your front line and the trenches you were digging?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that I only went three times, once to Zuc and two to Vogosca, and in the meantime I got on with my job, and that's when I was wounded. We were in Vogosca just ten to 15 metres away from the Serb front lines, by the communications faculty there. They said it was close by, but I don't really know myself because it was night-time and we had to dig silently. At Zuc the distance was even smaller.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us now, please, what the members of the BH Army were wearing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, they were wearing civilian clothes. People were wearing what they had. Some people would sew themselves a kind of uniform from some tent material and when I came out later on from the hospital, and they had uniforms. I had two sons who were in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What were your sons wearing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they first wore civilian clothes but towards the end of 1994, they were issued some sort of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what weapons the members of the BH Army had at the beginning and then later on?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you any details as to their weapons. All I can say is that my sons never brought any weapons home with them. And when I went trench digging, I just saw rifles, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the time you were trench digging, were there any casualties? Did any of your friends, any of the people you dug with, were they killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That night at Zuc, while we were digging the trenches, two men -- two of our men were killed. One was a driver, one was a worker.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When they were buried, were they buried -- given a military funeral? Were they buried as soldiers or as civilians?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. I was wounded soon after that, so I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. don't know anything about where they were buried or how. I know that one of them was very poor. He had a lot of children. But I really can't say where they were buried. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us yesterday that you went around town collecting up the rubbish. In Sarajevo, was there a special depot or dump where you took the rubbish to, and if so, could you tell us the route you took to reach it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was are road called Put Spasa, Salvation Road, and that went from my own company towards the bakery and the tobacco factory and behind the Marshal Tito barracks, and then you had to take the by-streets through town so that you were better protected. You couldn't take the main streets. So that's the route we took. And in 1992, they were -- drivers were taking rubbish there. They passed through some hangars and some things like that. I didn't actually go there myself. But later on, when this depot or dump was filled, they had to go via the wire factory. There was a large facility there before the war, and there was a ditch of some kind, and in 1997, we took the rubbish to the municipal depot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you drove to Stup hill.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't Stup hill. It was called Ravan, the foot of Stup hill, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never went there, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you also said that there was a shortage of water and electricity. As far as I recall, you said that there was no water or electricity in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, why there was no electricity? What was the reason for the electricity cut, if we know that there were soldiers and that fighting was going on. Why wasn't there any electricity?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's quite simple. All the long-distance communication lines supplying the town with electricity were shelled, so they were down. And the same applied to water. There was water shortage because the water facilities had been destroyed. And of course, there was shooting and fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please: If there was no water in Cengic Vila, the area that you lived in, what about Nedzarici and Grbavica? Would there be no water there too?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There wouldn't be.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, was the pattern the same for electricity? If in one part of town the electricity was down, would it be down in the other?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's right. The whole town would be left without water and electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the whole town," what do you mean by that? Do you include the Vogosca, Ilidza, Grbavica municipalities as well, Dobrinja, Nedzarici, and all the others, when you say "the whole town"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't mean those municipalities. I mean just the area that was held by our people. We really didn't have water and electricity. But when I did trench-digging at Zuc, you could see that there was electricity down there in Ilidza. It was night-time. We dug trenches at night. So you could see the electricity, the lights on down there. We were up on the hill, and you could see that they had electricity down there in the valley, and that was the area held by the Republika Srpska side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when we're talking about your part of town, Cengic Vila, the Cengic Vila district, Alipasino Polje, when there was no electricity there, could there have been electricity in Nedzarici, for example?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say. I think that they should have had electricity, but I'm not quite sure. I think they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. The Defence has no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown photograph P3244. That's the one he marked yesterday. And could it be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday you marked on that photograph a line which appears in front of you. The line appears to cross the street. Do you remember placing that line there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You explained to us that there was a wire which crossed the road. It was about a metre high at the road surface and rose to a height of about two and a half metres where it joined the building behind it. Is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you said that it had some covering draped over it. Do you remember what sort of covering it was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got there, when I got there to clear up the rubbish and load it up, and when I had finished loading the first truck, I was behind this building here, and as I was sitting up in the loader, I was behind the corner, and I would look behind to see whether anybody was passing and I noticed this wire and several blankets here on the pavement in this corner. So they were moving from here to there, to cover the entrance, and on this other building opposite. It was probably hitched up to that building too. There was a passageway leading towards the other buildings and pedestrians used to pass by that way. The wire was set quite high. You could just pass under it if you were in a small car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time you were shot, where was your vehicle in relation to the wire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My rear end was here. It's a little wider. And that's where it was. And I saw the wire from this part while I was waiting for Milan to bring up the truck for me to load up the rubbish. It was all very fast. Everything happened very quickly. But I do remember these two or three blankets, and they were torn.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. This morning you told us something of the incident where a woman was injured by a shell near your place in 1992, and you were asked whether you knew what the shell was targeting, what the target was. You replied that whenever they felt like it, they would press the trigger and fire. Who were you referring to when you said those words?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the Serb army, which was in the conflict and confrontation with the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Any questions from the Bench? Yes, please. Judge El Mahdi will put one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to ask you two questions. The first question I have in mind is in relation to the question you were asked about the shelling that took place in November, and then you said that it actually took place in the summer, in 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's possible -- I can't quite remember. It's possible that I made a mistake. Because a lot of time has passed, and many years, of course, and one forgets. But I believe that it is true what I said the first -- what I said in my first statement, because that was closer to the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You also said - and I am quoting - [In English]: "When a shell fell, another one followed." [Interpretation] And you said that this was in relation to the incident that happened in the summer in 1992, and that at the moment that your son went to help or to help with controlling the fire which resulted after the shelling, was there another shelling after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mention a fire. There was no fire. But the shell, when it landed, we were in the hallway on a building [as interpreted], and then the shell fell on the skyscrapers around Miljacka, and these young men went to help, and my son as well. And what is usually said is that one shell would follow another. There was a woman. I did not see her, but I did see my son. They were helping her, carrying her in, and then they took her away. And when these young men came back into the hallway of the building, they said that she was very seriously wounded. She was a young woman. And in fact, she was wounded very seriously in the stomach. That shell hit, and why and how, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this was just one shell?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, it was just one shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, in relation to the other incident - and I'm talking about when you were actually targeted - so if I understand correctly, you were wounded on the left hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if I understand correctly, you were trying to take cover, to escape, and you got off the loader on the left-hand side, on the side of your door.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You get in -- in normal conditions, you get in on the left and you get out on the left, but because the bullets were coming -- being fired from the left-hand side and then went out through the right-hand door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You went out -- you got off the loader the left or the right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got off on the right side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the right side.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When you sit in a loader, to us, this is -- one is left side, and that is the right side. So normally I got in on the left side, and that's how you get out, normally. You normally don't get out on the right side, because there is a tank, a fuel tank, and there are no steps that you can go down. But then from the fuel tank, I jumped off to the floor -- to the ground, and holding my hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But after the shots that hit you and wounded you, were there other shots being fired?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course there were. You can see that on the engine, on the loader. There were 64 shots fired just on the cabin, on the cabin alone, not counting the fuel tank, and my colleagues were talking about it afterwards. You could see it on the photograph yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you yourself did not see what was being called a nest of snipers?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. But the following day, when the French soldiers came to get the loader, that's when they saw that, and that's what I heard afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Velic -- Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd seek to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would seek to ask a few more questions as a result of the responses that the witness has just asked [sic]. I'll explain what it goes to. Mr. President, you and Your Honours may have noticed that during examination-in-chief I abandoned the line of questioning in relation to the shelling incident when the witness indicated it was summer rather than November of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. And the witness has just said that he abides by the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The November.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. November and the date in his statement. If it's accepted that he indicates November, I have nothing further to say; otherwise, I could show him his statement and clarify that point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just wanted to say that if the Prosecution would like to have another turn of questioning, another examination, then of course we would like to have another round the questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At earlier occasions I always gave the Defence an equal opportunity to ask additional questions when I gave it to the Prosecution, and that will be my line. So only if I forget it, please remind me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the reason why you asked for any further questioning, and having listened to what the witness testified, that he Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. would stick to the more precise date, I think there will be no reason specifically to ask any additional questions, so -- nor the Prosecution, but also not the Defence will have an opportunity to put additional questions to the witness. Mr. Velic, you've been answering for quite some time the questions put to you both by the Prosecution and by the Defence and also by the Judges. You'll understand that testimony of those who have been present during those days in that area are of great importance for this Tribunal, which will have to take decisions on events that happened at that time. I thank you very much for having come that long way to The Hague and I wish you a good journey home. Thank you very much

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, while the witness is being led out of the courtroom, we still have some admission of exhibits to do. As far as I can see, we have the video. That would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video will be Exhibit P3280D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we have the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a series of pictures of the front loader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we have another series of photos marked both during the moment when the statements were written down and in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These documents, I still forget one, and that's a medical -- yes, I've got it on my next page, a medical report, and a translations of it, that would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1806, P1806.1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and these are both double documents, and double translations as well. They are admitted into evidence. Mr. Ierace, your next witness is Witness I, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you for giving me the floor. Just to be -- just to be absolutely clear in relation to the transcript, on page 9, line 6, page 9, line 6, and the witness said, "In end of 1994," and this is not what was said in the English transcript. So I think it would be good to say that what he said was "end of 1994," just for the clarity of the transcript. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just find out exactly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could perhaps give you the references again. This is page 9, line 6, beginning of line 6, at 9.55, and I'm saying that because I will have -- it was 9 hours 13 minutes 55 seconds, it was about 1994. That was the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My colleague, Judge Nieto-Navia says that the transcript says that it's 1994. But I have some difficulties since the time on my laptop is not exactly the same as it is -- could you please indicate again the time? You said it was 9.13? Did I understand you well? I'll just do a quick search on "1994."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my current transcript on page 9, of the transcript, line 6, the first page at 9.13.55, I see "end of" and then I can read a word "sniefrn", but I believe that is about the -- numbers that are missing which are 1994. I'm not sure that you have the same transcript as I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that Judge Nieto-Navia is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I was checking my notes here and the witness said "1994," but I cannot see that in the transcript, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There will be people who will be working on it this weekend, and this is a provisional transcript, so this is just to specify clearly that the witness had said, "1994, end of."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both your recollection and the recollection Judge Nieto-Navia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Just for the transcript again, I said I was checking the transcript, I couldn't see that date, but in my notes, I had the date 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That being clarified, could we then have the next witness brought in? I think everything is prepared for the protective measures and the public gallery is empty at this moment. Please, would you bring in the next witness, Mr. Usher?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Protective measures have been granted in respect of you, and it means that we will not use your name but we'll call you Witness I. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration before the examination starts. The text will be now handed out to you by the usher. Would you please make that declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Witness I, you will be first examined by the Prosecution, and the examination, will it be Mr. Ierace or Mr. Mundis or -- please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should indicate at the outset that the relevant video to be shown to this witness has not yet been redacted. There has been some difficulties in getting access to the equipment. The equipment is located in a courtroom. Therefore, I propose that at the appropriate time, the video be shown in circumstances where it cannot be broadcast outside, and when a redacted version is available, I will seek to tender that without any qualification. In the meantime, I will seek to tender the unredacted version as a confidential exhibit. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown P3651.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please look at the piece of paper in front of you? Do not read it out loud, just read it to yourself, and can you confirm that the details on it as to your name and date of birth are correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might that -- Mr. President, I seek to tender that as a confidential exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3651 is admitted as sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, in 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before the armed conflict began in that year, what was your occupation, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I worked in a factory. It was an engine factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Following the commencement of hostilities, what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Locksmith.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you involved in the armed conflict in any way in the course of your employment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that year, 1992, did you know a woman with the surname of Dizdarevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was her full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Her name was Hajrija Dizdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By 1993, how long had you known her for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I knew her for some time, and then in 1993, throughout, I knew her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts did she live in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with her from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the reason for that? Were you friends or was there some particular reason to have contact with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: We are friends, and also through a pledge, because I gave a pledge to her son, who went to medical treatment, that I should look after her because she was an elderly lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how old was she in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: She was 78, about 78.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By July of 199' -- withdraw that. In July of 1993, was there anyone living with her in her apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How often would you see her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Every other day, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was the last time that you saw her alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: 16th of July, 1993, about 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you see her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: In her apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there anyone else present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. A friend of hers was present, Zlata Dzubur.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you left her, did she say anything as to what her plans were for the next day or so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. They agreed that the following day, on the 17th, that a friend would come at 9.00 for coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you understand that to be 9.00 in the morning or 9.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was the next time that you went to Mrs. Dizdarevic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: On the 17th of July, about 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: The neighbours met me, to talk to me, and to -- and they asked me where Hajrija was because they couldn't find her and she wasn't opening the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you do when you were told that, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: So what I did then was that, with a neighbour who was in charge of the building, I went to the next-door building, I went to the fifth floor and, in the next-door flat, I went from one balcony to another, I crossed over to another balcony, and I entered into her flat, into the flat of Hajrija Dizdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So you made your way across the outside of the building from the next-door flat into Mrs. Dizdarevic's flat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. It was quite a risky thing to do, because the apartment was facing the side from where the -- there was sniping, so I did it -- I took the risk and I crossed over from one balcony to another on the outside of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which room of Mrs. Dizdarevic's apartment did you enter first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: First I went into the living-room from the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you find Mrs. Dizdarevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You then looked through her apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. I checked the bedroom first, where she slept. I couldn't find her. So I went to another room, the second bedroom. She was not there. And the last room I checked was the kitchen, where I found her lying dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you describe, please, the manner in which she was lying? What position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: She was lying in such a way that her feet were below the window and the -- her head was opposite to the window. She was lying on her back with her hands on her chest, and she was -- and she was holding -- she was holding the beads, Muslim beads, in her hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, could you please demonstrate to the Trial Chamber the manner in which she was holding her hands on her chest? And perhaps you could slowly stand up before you do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: [Indicates] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President for the transcript, the witness has his elbows against the side of his body, his forearms raised at about 45 degrees with his hands clenched, not quite touching, in a position above his chest, and the clenched hands are not touching the wall of the chest. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please sit down again, sir. You said that she was holding Muslim beads. Did you know her to be of the Muslim faith?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you ever seen her praying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And either before or during or after prayers, had you seen her before with those beads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you tell us the circumstances in which you've seen her with the beads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: In the morning, usually. She would be with them around 8.00 in the morning, then around noon, that is, around 12.00, and then in the evening, around 7.00, 1900.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were they also the times that typically she would say her prayers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Well, that would be usually around 8.00 in the morning, around noon, 12.00, and 1900.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, had you previously seen her say her prayers in her apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what room or what rooms in her apartment had you seen that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: In the kitchen usually, or dining-room. I mean, that is just one area, one room, the kitchen and the dining-room.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was she wearing when you found her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: She had a skirt and a blouse, a dark skirt. The skirt was of a dark colour. And a blouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there any windows in the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: There were three windows. The one on the right-hand side was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "the right-hand side," is that as you stood in the kitchen looking out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did any of the windows in the kitchen have glass in them at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know why that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Because the glass had been broken following the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice on her any sign of any wound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please tell us what you saw in that regard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: When I came near her, I saw a wound in her right temple.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What sort of wound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: A bullet wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it that there was some blood, apart from the wound, elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. Very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Very little, did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Although there was no glass on the windows, was there any other form of covering across the window frames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What sort of covering was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: There was plastic sheeting, reinforced, because I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You put that up for her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any electricity in the apartment at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, had there been electricity available in the apartment on previous occasions that you had been there during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Now and then. The city was without electricity, and there would be some lights now and then only.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were any of the three windows in an open position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Only the one in the kitchen, and the one on the right in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the -- I withdraw that. Was the plastic sheeting -- I withdraw that. What degree of visibility was available through the plastic sheeting? Could you see clearly through it, as if it was glass? Was it totally transparent or was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Well, opaque grey plastic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've said that one of the windows was in an open position, that is, the one on the right. Was that slightly open, half open, completely open? What degree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Wide open.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From your knowledge at the time, having visited her regularly, did that expose an occupant of the kitchen to any danger by having a window wide open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please explain why.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Because this window faced Grbavica, the shopping centre, and Hrasno Brdo, and it is there that the forces of the Serb army -- from there that the forces of the Serb army acted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know whether, on any previous occasion, her apartment had received any fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. The interior walls were damaged and the window panes were shattered and broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say that the forces of the Serb army acted from those areas - from Grbavica, the shopping centre, and Hrasno Brdo - in what way did they act?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That was shelling and sniper fire and so-called death sowers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "death sowers," what type of fire or weapon is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: It is a firearm with, as far as I know about it, with high velocity per second, high velocity of fire per second.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: After you discovered the body of your friend, did you -- when you left the apartment, how did you do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I found the keys. I tripped over them, because it was dark. But I stumbled across them and I just -- I opened the door and locked the door, told the neighbours that she had been killed, and then I locked it again, without letting anyone in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to that answer, you needed the keys to unlock the door in order to leave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you gained entry via a neighbour's apartment. Had anyone tried to open her door, her front door, that is, from the outside, so that entry could be gained that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not have a key that would fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any other means of entrance to the apartment apart from that door or via the outside of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: The only way was the way that I used to enter, or to break the door down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And was the way you used to enter by coming in through that same door that you exited through on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In September -- I withdraw that. What was the weather like on the day -- on that day, on the evening of which you found Mrs. Dizdarevic's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: The weather was fair. It was sunny.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the weather like the day before, that is, the 16th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Again, fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I seek to show the video, which is Exhibit 3280B. And again, I'd be grateful if that could be shown in private session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have the exhibit marked as P3280E; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then go into private session before showing the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. President, I should ask one question first. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll wait for one second with private session and ... Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In September of last year, did you attend the apartment where Mrs. Dizdarevic had lived in the company of an investigator and some camera people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you notice that there had been some changes to the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll now enter into private session, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see it's on my screen now that there's no "PS" any more, so we're in open session now. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked to indicate where the chair was. Could you tell us in your own words how you found that chair to be when you entered the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I suppose that as Hajrija was falling, being hit by this bullet, she must have also caught this chair, which would have been standing normally, and as she was falling, she pulled it, but the table was in the way, so that the chair was tilted at an angle of 45 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you regularly visited her in that apartment. Over what period of time before then? A matter of weeks, months, or longer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Well, it was while her son was still there, but -- that is, from the beginning of the war, because the son was very seriously ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you ever known any Bosnian government defence forces to occupy that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you ever observed any defence forces in the vicinity of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. building, that is, around the outside of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: No. No. There was no front line there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown an exhibit, in particular, the -- excuse me. Exhibit P3216, which is a collection of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I forgot to put on the microphone. Could you please distribute it to -- first give it to -- you have got copies, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is no identification issues with the photographs themselves so they may be placed -- they will be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will start off with photograph 1A, and I'll lead so that I can save time. Unless and until my friends object.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is photograph 1A a view taken from the inside of Mrs. Dizdarevic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And perhaps the photograph might be taken off the ELMO for a moment and handed to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please turn the photograph over? And do you see on the back, your signature and the date, being the 22nd of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And as the apartment appears in the photograph, particularly the kitchen, does it appear to have been redecorated since the time that you found Mrs. Dizdarevic's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is the window space the same as it was at the time that you found her body, in particular the window on the right, which appears in the open position in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Except that the window pane is proper, glass panes have been put in and everything has been put in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please look at photo 1B, if that could be placed on the ELMO? Did you indicate three things on photo 1B with a red pen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does A indicate the particular window that was open when you found Mrs. Dizdarevic's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does C indicate the chair that you saw in a tilted position at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does the area within the circle marked B indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Well, that is the opening, the aperture, of the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to photo 2A. Does that appear to be another view through the window of Mrs. Dizdarevic's kitchen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And have you placed markings -- I withdraw that. Please place photograph 2B on the ELMO. Now, by comparing photographs 2A and 2B, in order to get a clearer view of what appeared through the window, can you indicate, if you know, where the building circled and marked letter A is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I can't quite figure it out, but I think that this is the building housing the shopping centre at Grbavica. That is the line that was held by the Serb troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the two buildings marked -- withdraw that. In relation to the three buildings marked with the letter B, are you able to say, firstly, whether those buildings existed at the time that Mrs. Dizdarevic was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And secondly, which side of the confrontation line those buildings were on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: These buildings were on the first confrontation line, that is on the Bosnian Army line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please now look at photo 3A? Could that be placed on the ELMO? Do you agree that that appears to be either a telephoto shot or a blowup of part of the earlier photograph, 2A? In other words, it shows the view through the window in more detail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And would you now go to photo 3B? I draw your attention firstly to the building that you have marked with a circle and then placed hatch marks within the circle. Do you know the name of that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That is -- it is called Loris building, because the shop is called Loris.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. I don't know whether Mr. Ierace has told us whether it was the witness who circled this building or made any other markings. And perhaps it was one of those things that the Chamber would not like to see because they were previously marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is nothing against previously marked photographs, but your question suggested that the markings were made by the witness. Could you please first ask him before you proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. President, just a moment. We were talking here regarding possible incident concerning these photographs. I hope that the Prosecution will help us so that can we examine what is significant here. Perhaps we shall be coming back to this. I hope we shall have 30 seconds in order to be able to ascertain that, because I believe that time is right now for the break, and we can resolve it during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I just ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but I did understand you well? You're talking about the relevance of this part of the evidence? Is that what I understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. It will be too much to say relevance. I'm talking about significance inter partes regarding these documents. That is, I'm referring to the fair trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid at this moment -- one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If I do understand you well, you want to raise an issue perhaps during the break with the Prosecution and we will then hear whether this will have any result. Please be very careful in reporting of your discussions, since this has caused some difficulties now and then. So mind your words and we'll then have a break. Mr. I, we'll have a break until 11.00, and then your examination will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you're at ease, as I see. Is there anything to be reported?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. We were examining the issues with the Prosecution. The letter that we received was not clear enough, but of course orally Mr. Ierace was able to explain to us what it was about, and we're making greater headway now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm quite happy that you were able to solve the problem. Mr. Ierace, then we can proceed with the examination of the witness. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in Witness I. You may proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, on a number of these photographs there are - on the photocopies, that is, the black-and-white versions - markings with a red pen on the surface of the photographs themselves. Those markings comprise letters of the alphabet, circles, lines, and arrows. Who placed them on those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, coming back to photograph 3B, which is on the machine to your right, you have circled and crossed a building, only one building. Do you know the name of that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: The Loris building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How close was that building to the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: It is at the confrontation line itself, and the line was held by the army of Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to that answer, do I take it that everything which appears beyond that building was in the control of the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also marked a building with the letter "A" and a circle. Do you know what type of construction that was, in other words, whether it was a business building of some description, commercial nature, or residence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: A residential building, a skyscraper at the shopping centre location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the shopping centre have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: It is in the Grbavica district.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please now go to photograph 4A, and that is now displayed before you. Was that also a view from the window of the deceased's kitchen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We see different things in that photograph to what we saw in the earlier views. Was that to the left or to the right of what we have seen previously through the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the copy - and perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO - we see that you have marked two areas: "A" and "B." What is the area within the circle marked "A"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That is the front line held by the Serb army, that is to say, Hrasno, the hills around the stadium, Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Indeed, I think on the colour version of that photograph, we can see what appear to be some lights on a pillar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Look at the colour version of the photograph, and do you see that immediately to the left of the metal window frame there appears to be a construction in the form of a white tower with an object which is rectangular in shape on top of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. That's the chimney from the boiler house, in the Hrasno district, Trg, Trg Heroje, Heroes' Square.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the metal pointer, could you please point to the chimney. Could you please point to the photograph that's to your right rather than the photograph on the screen. The usher will show you which photograph to point to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. I, will you point at that picture. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. That is the chimney. Now, if you move the pointer to the right. Please move your pointer to the right. Yes. Just stop there for a moment. If you could just keep the pointer still. All right. Now move the pointer a little further to the right, where there is what appears -- Yes. Now, do you see that just beneath the white tip of the pointer on the photograph there appears to be a white column with a rectangular object on top of it? If you take away the tip of the pointer, you should be able to see it immediately beneath it. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: They're the floodlights from the Zeleznicar stadium at Grbavica. It was a football stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where was the stadium in relation to the confrontation lines at the time that Mrs. Dizdarevic was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: In the hands of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please now go to the left of the chimney, and on the black-and-white photograph, you have marked that area with a circle and the letter "B." What is that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That is the line at Grbavica held by the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. So by way of summary, behind the various buildings that we see in that photograph, that is the high-rise buildings, we see a ridge with smaller dwellings upon it and trees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, please go to photograph 5A and look at that one. Do you recognise the apartment block which appears in the centre of that photograph and occupies most of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which building is that one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That is the building in which the late Hajrija lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to the black-and-white photocopy. Have you marked the building in which she lived with the letter "A"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: The letter "A," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You have circled and marked a portion of another building on the margin of the photograph with the letter "B." What significance does that building have? A[redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please now go to photograph 6A? Having regard to your earlier answer, is that also a photograph of the building in which Mrs. Dizdarevic lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please look at the black-and-white photocopy, and in particular, the area of the facade that is marked with the letter "A."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you allow me to confer for just one second with Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I draw to your attention especially to the protective measures, Mr. Ierace? At least in view of one of your last questions and one of the indications that - we will have the proper Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. redactions prepared. Would you please keep that in mind while showing photos to the witness and asking questions about them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On photograph 6B, which appears in front of you, there is an area of the facade of the deceased's building which is marked with the letter "A." What does that area signify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: That is the apartment belonging to the late Hajrija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see on that photograph the kitchen window that you observed to be open when you discovered her body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. And I have marked it with a "B."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The area marked with the letter "C" appears to be, at least in part, an adjoining apartment. Is that the apartment through which you exited in order to gain entry to the deceased's apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please now go to photograph 7A. Does 7A show a closeup of the exterior of the deceased's apartment, in particular part of her balcony and the kitchen area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes, the kitchen window and the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you marked the kitchen window that was open at the relevant time with the letter "A"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please now turn to photograph 8A. Again, does the letter "B" depict the kitchen window that was open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does "A" depict the deceased's veranda and the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does "C" depict the part of the neighbour's apartment which you used to gain access to the deceased's apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, during the armed conflict, did you lose any members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who were they? Which members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: My wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the cause of her death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: A shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What side of the confrontation lines was she on at the time of her death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: She was on the line held by the Bosnian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you content to be living on the Bosnian government side of the confrontation lines during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. It's my town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you aware of other individuals of Serbian background who chose to live in Sarajevo on the same side of the confrontation lines during the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take you back to the clothing that the deceased was wearing when you found her. You've told us that you've told us about the dress that she was wearing, the blouse that she was wearing. Did you see any signs of headgear, if not necessarily on her, as she lay on the ground, but perhaps nearby? By "headgear," I mean any item of head clothing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I think she had a scarf, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the occasions that you had observed her to be praying, according to her faith, had you noticed whether she typically wore any headgear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes. She would wear a scarf. She would always wear a scarf when she was praying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is the Defence ready for cross-examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, let me start off by wishing you good day and thanking you for coming. I shall be asking you questions in French, and I know that they will be perfectly interpreted. Witness, you said, in answer to a question put to you this morning, that your professional qualifications were that of a mechanic, locksmith; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Having asked you that question, the Prosecution went on to ask you whether you were implicated in the armed conflict in any way, whether you were involved in the course of your employment, and your answer was no. Do you confirm that now? Do you confirm your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I do. I did not take part in the war, but I did do digging. I did trench-digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you now whether, in keeping with your testimony, whether you were interviewed by a representative of the Prosecution. And if your answer is yes, could you tell us what date that was exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood you. Do you mean here in the Tribunal now? Do you mean now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I mean well before you came here. Before you came to the Tribunal, did anybody interview you, question you, and did you give a statement, one or more than one, written statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did that in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that one of those statements is dated, according to what I'm reading, the 22nd of June, 2001, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes, it was June, yes, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Chamber grants permission, Mr. President, I should like perhaps to read a portion from one of the statements given by the witness, but I should first of all like to ask him whether he has read and signed his declarations -- statements, sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS I
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am going to quote, and I apologise in advance, Mr. President -- I'm just about to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has the statements in front of them so that they can follow your quotations. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am quoting from document ERN 03041571, and I'm going to quote in a language that is not my own native language, to help the witness understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said the following: "I worked in --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think that the document from which my friend is quoting is not the English statement.
